content: {"rule":"K-S2","applies":"yes","applies_why":"The judge text uses divergent answers about a single verse, Matthew 1:20, as the reason for UNDERDETERMINED, which is the kind of single-verse openness the rule forbids.","verdict":"BREACH","quote":"D2 vs C1 (Matthew 1:20): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the conception agency as covenant presence in [DR3] and defender answered the physical source in the womb in [CR2] and [CR3].","rule_words":"That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.","room":"A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.: reading one, the two answers make Matthew 1:20 open/UNDERDETERMINED; reading two, both senses must stand and the verse is not open.","why":"The judge labels Matthew 1:20 UNDERDETERMINED because the challenger and defender gave different senses, contrary to the rule that such a verse is not open and both senses stand."}
